latest.title: Mycelium–Photopolymer Hybrid Materials: Interface Formation, Growth, Moisture and Structural Performance
latest.summary: Mycelium-based living materials derive function from fungal growth through and across a shaped matrix. In printed hybrids, colonisation, moisture and nutrient transport, interfacial bridging and the evolving mechanical state are inseparable. This review treats the fungal phase as an active structural constituent whose morphology changes after fabrication, and it distinguishes printing fidelity from the later material state produced by growth. A qualification framework is proposed for species identity, growth conditions, interface formation, moisture dependence, mechanical development, contamination and regenerative behaviour. ER-433.

items.title: Emergence from Quantum Uncertainty: Testing a Novel Organizing Principle Using Neural Networks
items.summary: The functioning of complex natural systems, such as living systems, still lacks a generally accepted theoretical basis and respective empirical verification. We propose an experiment to test whether such systems are subject to a hitherto unknown organizing principle, in which the quantum mechanical uncertainty principle enables ordering phenomena in chaotic or nearly chaotic systems in the sense of a strong emergence principle. Contrary to previous proposals, our hypothesis does not require fragile macroscopic quantum coherence, ensuring compatibility with the harsh conditions in living systems. items.title: The Pauli Spin Algebra, Related Clifford Algebra Representation and the Dirac Hamiltonian Operator Derivation
items.summary: I present a novel approach to derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian operator on the secondly quantized Fock space, based on the the Pauli spin \(\text{su}{(2)}\) - algebra and its Clifford algebra representation. The relativistic Lorentz invariance of the related Schrödinger equation is stated as a natural consequence of its operator structure.

items.title: Quantum Biology 2.0: Traversing and harnessing protein superhighway networks of light and life.
items.summary: As an emergent field stimulated by insights from the biological, chemical, physical, and quantum sciences, quantum biology explores how quantum phenomena such as superradiance, tunneling, and entanglement can be leveraged to enhance, influence, and probe biological processes across a diversity of scales and physical degrees of freedom. This review surveys key theoretical, computational, and experimental developments over the last decade, providing relevant historical background and scientific context going back as far as Bohr's 1932 lecture on "Light and Life" in Copenhagen. items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: A Survey
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to turn gains in an AI system into a stronger capacity to produce subsequent gains. Foundation models make parts of this process practical through generated training data, program revision and automated experimentation, but repeated optimization alone does not establish recursive improvement. This survey organizes the field around two overlapping goals: automated design of AI infrastructure, and repair and optimization of existing systems. We relate these goals to AutoML, meta-learning and program search, and formulate their objectives alongside criteria for task gains, retained capabilities and improved update procedures. items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry explains many structural features of real-world networks, yet existing hyperbolic generative network models with community organization such as the nonuniform popularity-similarity optimization (nPSO) are restricted to unipartite graphs. Here we introduce a bipartite extension of the nPSO model called nBPSO, motivated by the prevalence of community organization in real-world bipartite networks and the emerging evidence of hyperbolic hierarchical connectivity in trained sparse neural networks. nBPSO provides explicit control over link density, degree distribution, average clustering, and community organization. items.title: Experimental platform to study the neuronal mechanisms of magnetoreception in the honey bee.
items.summary: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) offer an alternative model for investigating magnetoreception, exhibiting reliable navigation and behavioral responses to magnetic fields. Thanks to their compact brains, well-matched to the penetration depth of modern optical imaging techniques, they may offer insights into the neural and biochemical mechanisms underlying this sense, something that standard models, like migrating birds, have not so far provided. But also in honeybees, this progress requires tools capable of resolving weak, magnetically induced neural activity with high spatio-temporal precision. items.title: Toward quantum-informed addiction medicine: Coherence, entangled-photon imaging, and a theranostic hypothesis.
items.summary: Background Quantum biology has shown that selected biological processes depend on quantum effects, including coherence, tunnelling, and spin-dependent reactions. In parallel, quantum imaging now uses entangled photons to extract biological information at low photon flux. Early evidence that biological tissue can alter photon entanglement in disease-associated ways raises a translational question: whether decoherence itself can become a diagnostic signal. items.title: Beyond the Superintelligent Machine: A Systems Definition of Superintelligence for the Era of Agentic AI
items.summary: Superintelligence is usually defined as a machine intellect that exceeds human cognition across most domains. That framing conflates three distinct properties: computational capability, warranted knowledge, and legitimate authority. This article develops a systems definition suited to large language models, tool-using agents, databases, theorem provers, and other computational knowledge artifacts. Using conceptual synthesis and constructive requirement derivation, we distinguish a computational artifact, an operational self that preserves commitments and consequence history, and a normative principal that holds purpose and accountability. items.summary: We study the geometry of the Poincaré ball equipped with a rotationally symmetric metric \(g_\eta\) conformally close to the hyperbolic metric \(g_{\mathbb{H}}\), with curvature pinched in \([-1-\eta, -1+\eta]\). items.title: Bayesian Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agent not only to acquire new knowledge and capabilities, but also to reason about which existing capabilities remain valid, when they should be routed, tested, retained, deprecated, restructured, or replaced, and whether the mechanisms governing these decisions should themselves be modified. items.title: HieFormer: Leveraging hyperbolic geometry to overcome the hierarchical expressiveness limitation of transformers.
items.summary: 3D instance segmentation requires fine-grained geometric discrimination together with an effective representation of the hierarchical organization of real-world objects and scenes. Conventional transformer architectures, however, operate predominantly in Euclidean space, whose polynomial volume growth can be poorly matched to strongly tree-like structures and can contribute to feature crowding in cluttered scenes. items.title: HyperCLIP++: Fine-Tuning CLIP for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Hyperbolic Space.
items.summary: CLIP, a foundational vision-language model, has emerged as a powerful tool for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. items.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.
items.summary: Human conscious thought often appears as a diffuse, unstable, and only partly verbalizable field until attention, questioning, decision, or speech stabilizes it into a reportable form. This manuscript develops a quantum-inspired neural framework for that transition. The proposal does not claim that consciousness literally depends on microscopic quantum computation, that the brain implements a physical quantum computer, or that neuronal tissue maintains macroscopic quantum coherence. items.title: Quantum coherent dynamics in allophycocyanin trimer complex.
items.summary: For years, scientists have debated whether plants and algae use quantum coherence to enhance the transfer of light energy during photosynthesis. Some studies have suggested that wavelike quantum effects might help energy flow more efficiently between pigments. To investigate this idea, we studied allophycocyanin (APC), a light-harvesting protein complex found in cyanobacteria. Using a combination of ultrafast laser spectroscopic methods and rigorous hierarchical equations-of-motion simulations, we examined both the trimer protein complex and its monomer subunit.
